title: Vintage Gibson ES-335 Value Guide: Prices By Year To 1979
description: ES-335 values from $3,000 to $70,000 across researched eras, plus the site's wider dot-neck anchor. Compare years, finishes, tailpieces and repairs.
alt: Sunburst Gibson ES-335 with dot inlays, two covered pickups and a stopbar in a pink-lined case

faqs.q: How Much Is A Vintage Gibson ES-335 Worth?
faqs.a: Vintage Gibson ES-335 reference values run from $3,000 to $5,500 for typical 1970s examples to $33,000 to $70,000 across the researched early dot-neck sales, reviewed in October 2026. My existing site guide gives the broader all-original dot-neck market as $30,000 to $80,000+, so the research band below isn't a ceiling for a rare or exceptional guitar.

faqs.q: Does A Natural Finish Use The Sunburst Range?
faqs.a: No. Original natural-finish early ES-335s are excluded from the ordinary sunburst and cherry research group. They need finish-specific sale evidence.

faqs.q: Why Is The 1968 Figure Different From 1969?
faqs.a: The 1968 row retains the site's $7,000 to $8,000 clean-original anchor. The 1969 row uses a played-original research group and marks the multi-piece neck and shorter tenon transition. Condition and construction both differ.

faqs.q: Does A Refinish Change Gibson ES-335 Value?
faqs.a: Yes. The ranges assume the original finish described in each era's notes. A full refinish needs matching altered-guitar sales. Published Les Paul deductions provide context, but they are not measured Gibson ES-335 discounts.

faqs.q: How Can I Get My Gibson ES-335 Appraised?
faqs.a: Send clear front and back photographs, both sides of the headstock, the pickups, bridge, case and any known repairs. Keep removed original parts with the instrument and include the history you know. Those details support an individual appraisal.
